messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High failure rate exporting traces via OTLP -> New Relic (service=auth-service). Error surfacing in collector logs. Auto-incident RED-4720 created.
Maya: I'm on it. initial triage: are spans still emitted? or completely lost upstream?
Samir: spans generated locally. otel-collector pods show `exporter: send failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed` and many retries. no downstream 5xx on prod APIs.
Liu: grabbing logs from collectors in eu-west1. snippet:
```
2024-06-13T09:10:24Z otel-collector[1]: exporter/newrelic: failed to export: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
2024-06-13T09:10:24Z otel-collector[1]: exporter/newrelic: queuing 3123 spans to memory buffer
```
Samir: seeing similar in us-east1 and ap-south1. memory buffer grown to ~9M spans across cluster.
Maya: check disk buffering config? we shipped file_buffer but not enabled in all clusters. can we toggle file buffer and set up BigQuery/S3 backfill exporter?
Liu: yes we have file exporter available. will flip it cluster-by-cluster. applying to us-east1 canary (2 pods) now.
ops-bot: NOTE: added temporary alert collector-buffer-memory > 75% -> page eng-oncall.
newrelic-bot: New Relic Status: Partial Degradation impacting Trace ingest (https://status.newrelic.com/incidents/NR-2024-06-13-otlp). Investigating egress failures.
Samir: vendor status visible. escalate via enterprise channel for ETA. Maya can you open a support escalation with NR?
Maya: escalated via enterprise support channel. ticket NR-98765 opened. attaching collector logs.
Support Bot: Notifying affected customers with premium SLAs via templated email: "We are seeing delays and missing traces due to an upstream vendor ingestion problem. We are buffering locally and will forward once vendor ingestion recovers."
Liu: canary checks: file exporter is writing to /var/otel-buffer and collector doesn't OOM. memory buffer reduced by 60% in canary. will roll to remaining pods in 5 minutes.
Samir: add tail-sampling rule to preserve spans where error=true or http.status_code >= 500. we want to ensure error flows kept at 100%.
Maya: applying tail-sampling rule and sanitizer to drop PII before flush. note: some customers asked explicitly to prevent PII spillover; we'll skip forwarding for those until legal ok.
Liu: running `kubectl -n observability patch cm otel-config --patch "$(cat canary-fallback.yaml)"` and then restart collectors.
Samir: quick config snippet for runbook saved to incident ticket RED-4720:
```
exporters:
  file:
    path: /var/otel-buffer/spans.ndjson
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: preserve-errors
        trace_identifiers: { }
        decision_wait: 10s
        rules:
          - action: keep
            condition:
              numeric_attribute:
                key: http.status_code
                op: GE
                value: 500
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [tail_sampling]
      exporters: [file, newrelic]
```
Maya: also added disk-monitor cron to avoid full disk: `*/2 * * * * root df -h /var/otel-buffer || systemctl restart otel-collector` (temporary).
ops-bot: Escalation: enterprise channel message sent to New Relic with attached packet capture.
newrelic-bot: Update: We have identified an upstream CDN configuration issue causing intermittent TLS failures between NR ingestion edge and some customers egress IPs. Patch rolling; next update in 10m.
Liu: starting controlled flush attempts from canary to verify successful exports. seeing intermittent successes: `exporter/newrelic: exported 78 spans, result=success` at 09:23UTC but then another failure.
Samir: retain incident until buffers drained and we have >= 5m of steady success across regions. set severity SEV3 (no customer API outages).
Maya: handoff notes for next oncall -> RED-4720 current state: file buffering enabled cluster-wide, tail-sampling applied (errors=100%, others=5%), scrubber enabled, vendor escalated NR-98765, monitoring alerts for buffer-disk > 70% and collector-restart on crash.
Liu: added a small script to incident ticket that prints pending buffer counts per node every 60s: `for n in $(nodes); do ssh $n "ls -1 /var/otel-buffer | wc -l"; done` + logs to S3.
Support Bot: Customer comms updated: added note to premium customer page about delayed traces and that we will retry backfill once vendor allows.
Maya: legal callback: ensure we don't replay traces for customers who opted-out of replay. created list and added filter to scrubber to drop these customer IDs before forward.
Samir: if disk across collectors > 85% escalate scale-up: `kubectl scale deploy/otel-collector --replicas=12 -n observability` and notify infra.
newrelic-bot: Update: CDN vendor pushed fix; we've seen a drop in failures. ingestion rate returning to normal in most regions.
Liu: seeing sustained successes now (09:45UTC). logs show repeated `exported X spans, result=success`. buffer backlog decreasing from ~9M -> 1.2M and dropping.
Maya: monitoring CPU/disk during catch-up. we might need to rate-limit backfill to avoid overloading vendor. adding backfill throttle at 1000 spans/s per node.
Samir: noted for postmortem: - add multi-exporter fallback (mirror to S3/BigQuery), - synthetic OTLP ingest tests per region, - enforce per-vendor contract SLA for egress path, - document scrub/replay policy.
Support Bot: Incident severity updated to RESOLVED-PROLONGED -> when buffer < 1000 across all nodes and > 30m of stable exports.
Maya: handing off to Samir for overnight watch. Samir owns postmortem with timeline and remediation items.
Samir: acknowledged. I'll produce a timeline, root cause (CDN misconfig egress/TLS), mitigation steps applied, customer impact summary, and follow-ups (runbook updates + contract ask).
incidents-bot: Incident RED-4720 updated: status=monitoring, owner=Samir, linked vendor incident NR-2024-06-13-otlp.
Maya: thanks team. closing note: no customer-facing errors observed but observability gaps existed; buffering and sampling reduced signal loss for errors. :white_check_mark:
